purpose: Bounded native reference-to-controller diagnostic on existing qualified TRAIN recoveries; not a benchmark or policy evaluation.

cases.name: straight
cases.selection: first post-recovery 1-second window with speed at least 4 m/s and absolute yaw rate at most 0.08 rad/s

cases.name: steady_turn
cases.selection: first post-recovery 1-second window with speed at least 4 m/s and absolute yaw rate at least 0.25 rad/s and constant sign

selection_rule: Post-recovery means at least 80 ticks after takeover. Selection is based only on source kinematics and requires 2 seconds of comparison plus a complete 10-second teacher future before terminal braking. No fallback or outcome-based selection.
reference_clock: At simulation tick i use source tick i and its next 200 actual recorded states, regardless of progress divergence; no nearest-path rematching, time warping, or extrapolation. Transform source positions, velocities and accelerations to the current actual ego frame. PP uses current actual speed. PP arms use production mission_brake on current state and progress. pp_steer takes acceleration from recorded teacher controls before this override; pp uses PP acceleration. Teacher arm remains unchanged NativeExpert. op_steer uses unchanged OpenpilotFollower steering with recorded acceleration before mission_brake; this is a mapping diagnostic, not a learned-policy evaluation.

repeat_gate.contacts: exact source count at every tick

gate_policy: For every case, recorded controls from reset through comparison window must pass before any teacher or PP arm is run. Failure stops the experiment; no contract claim.
render: Cameras and initial reset rendering are enabled exactly as collection; after reset no camera captures or rendering occur in any arm. Recorded-control and teacher replay gates must pass before conclusions. This tests physical state reproducibility under omitted captures and does not claim camera equivalence.
limits: Time-indexed reference may move ahead of a lagging vehicle; this tests that declared bridge, not a progress-matched tracker or learned policy. Native repeat is checked in recorded planar state and contacts; hidden wheel state is reconstructed by replay, not measured or proven identical. Windows are short and selected training examples; no generalization or mission-completion claim. Replay tolerances are predeclared engineering limits, not calibrated simulator noise bounds. Runtime, source, scene and physics must match; fail closed on mismatch. Per-process wall-clock timeout is 900 seconds; an incomplete run is not evidence of a control outcome. The gate covers the nine recorded planar/actuator state columns and contacts; full native wheel, chassis 3D and hidden physics state are reconstructed but unobserved. The small tolerances are a stringent predeclared reproducibility gate, not a proven bound on hidden state.
diagnostics: Report both same-clock error and nearest-source-progress positional error; nearest progress is diagnostic only, using the finite selected source window, never to select reference or hide clock error.
teacher_gate: Teacher actuation must satisfy the same full-window state and contact repeat thresholds against the recorded source. Failure stops before follower arms and makes the bridge outcome inconclusive; teacher-versus-recorded action errors are also reported.
prefix_gate: Every intervention process separately passes the repeat thresholds and exact contacts from tick 0 through handoff before it may branch.
interpretation: After both gates pass, report fixed-clock action and trajectory errors plus contacts and referee state for each arm. Compare isolated steering arms to teacher, and full PP separately. These describe the tested windows; they are not an acceptance threshold for a vehicle or a causal proof of every failure.
